title: Does anybody else hate the expression “this movie was better than it had any right to be”?

commenti.body: It’s a pretentious way to say “I had prejudices about the broad strokes of this movie. But after secretly enjoying it, I toed the water and found that enough people in my social circles also enjoyed it for me to be open about it.”

Wow, that was really well put. 

“I liked it more than I thought I would,” would be a perfectly acceptable thing to say, but that would be admitting they had a predisposed judgement as you mentioned.

The phrase OP used puts the onus back on the filmmakers, as though everything every filmmaker makes has to somehow “deserve” to be liked.

Just classic narcissism cloaked as informed criticism.

not at all. it provides the context that they thought the movie would be shit, but it turned out not to be. maybe i feel similarly, whether it be due to the director, the cast, the marketing or whatever else. so that context is helpful

you sound like one of those people who get irate over the term "underrated" too

> The phrase OP used puts the onus back on the filmmakers,

yes, and possibly for legitimate reasons.

if a movie has a odd director choice, or a director who only made flops, or if the movie had a hectic production, then the natural expectation of that movie being good would be a lower. 

idk i just think the phrase shines some context that could be helpful for others who also had low expectations.

I think it can refer to movies that contain ideas that sound bad on paper, but are executed well enough to be surprisingly good. An example would be Swiss Army Man which centers around a farting corpse, but somehow ends up telling a poignant and beautiful story.

It could also mean that the film rose above circumstances that should have done it in. Did a film that was cobbled together from a rejected TV pilot and some added material from a year later have any idea to become one of the most beloved classics of this century? Perhaps Mulholland Drive was better than it had any right to be.

Eh, not really. It’s just another way to say something is “greater than the sum of its parts” or “punching above its weight” to me. Some movies (or other media) are like that, whether it’s because of the way it’s presented/previewee, or because of the people involved, or the lack of budget, etc. Like, I think the Power Rangers movie from 2017 is “better than it had any right to be”. While not the greatest movie, the fact that it tried to be a more serious, gritty Hollywood blockbuster while still capturing the spirit of Power Rangers and having quite a bit of heart to the characters makes it better than it had any right to be to me

I think it’s mostly about expectations. I found myself repeating that over and over when watching Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl.

I wasn’t expecting much. At that time, licensed properties had a pretty spotty and mostly negative reputation. So to be ‘good’ it just had to mediocre. But it was better than mediocre-it was great! Great dialogue, great score, good cinematography, good acting. 

What I expected was something more like ‘Sky High’ - a fun, but forgettable movie that’s kinda corny. If ‘Black Pearl’ was like ‘Sky High,’ I would have been completely satisfied. But it was BETTER! For me, it was better than it had to be

I mean, any qualitative comment on a film is subjective by nature, and any aspect that isn't cast/crew/logistics-based of any assessment is going to be biased by any number of things, including expectation. All this phrase is saying is that based on the known cast, crew, logistics, and/or marketing material, there was a high likelihood for a not-great result... and then it turned out otherwise. I don't take issue with that at all.

Some examples that involve exactly zero pretension that immediately pop into mind are:

1) If I said, "You should check out this zombie movie made by a handful of 20-somethings for $6,000 on a Canon 5DmkII and two lenses, shot in 15 days, and the writer/director is also one of the main characters," I think most would have a pretty clear picture in their head of what to expect, and it understandably wouldn't be great. But after watching *The Battery*, I think the phrase in question would be wildly appropriate.

2) Same too for, "We're gonna watch the second of two German films about necrophilia!" I think that what *Nekromantik 2* accomplishes as a film absolutely transcends its subject matter, and by extension the grand majority of people's expectations and prejudgements, and The Phrase is more than fitting.

I get it, i just don’t like the phrasing and there are better ways to say that.

Lmao no, no issues with underrated, under appreciated, under seen etc lol
